<action type="say">
Water still running is the most urgent issue—focus on stopping flow first:

1) Try to stop the water:
- Lift the toilet tank lid carefully.
- Reach in and lift the FLOAT (the plastic ball or cup that rises with the water) straight up. This should stop the water from refilling.
- If there’s a chain to the flapper (rubber seal at the bottom), you can also push the flapper down firmly to seal it while holding the float up with your other hand or propping it up with something (a stick/wooden spoon).

2) If water still won’t stop:
- Go to your main water shutoff:
  - Often in a closet, garage, or where water line enters the house.
  - Outside, sometimes by the street under a metal or plastic cover.
- Turn the main valve clockwise until it stops, even if it’s stiff. Use a wrench or pliers if you have them and it’s safe to do so.

3) Prevent more damage:
- Unplug or move anything electrical on the floor nearby.
- Use towels, blankets, or a mop to block water from spreading into other rooms.
- Put any important items off the floor.

I tried to locate an emergency plumber through this system but there are no providers available for your address right now. You’ll need to call someone directly:

- Search on your phone for: “24 hour emergency plumber Austin 78701”

  - Good rating, but right now speed matters most
- When you call, say:

“Hi, I’m at 123 Tech Park Drive, Austin 78701. A toilet overflowed, there was water on the floor, and I had to shut off the main at the curb, so the whole place has no water. I need a licensed plumber today, as soon as possible.

• What is your service/dispatch fee?  
• What is your hourly labor rate?  
• Do you charge an emergency/after‑hours fee?  
• Can you give me a rough price range for a toilet overflow/main shutoff situation before you start?  
• Are there any other fees I should expect?”

Pick the plumber who:
- Can arrive within the next few hours
- Clearly answers pricing questions (gives real numbers, not “it depends” only)
- Confirms they’re licensed/insured and serves downtown Austin

Before they start:
- Confirm: “So before you begin, can you confirm the service call fee and your expected total range if it’s a standard repair vs worst case?”
- Ask for a written or texted estimate if possible.
